kf1.tip: Imagine Dickens wrote that the winter weather froze Scrooge's features. Say what the reader would lose compared with "The cold within him froze his old features".
kf1.note: A strong answer sees that the weather version makes Scrooge a victim of outside conditions. "The cold within him" puts the coldness inside his own character, so he is responsible for it. That coldness is so powerful it shapes his face, nipping his nose and shrivelling his cheek. Most would say the reader loses the sense that Scrooge's nature is the problem. If you only said the original is more descriptive, you missed this shift from weather to character.

kf2.tip: Write the exam question that Marley's "Mankind was my business" helps answer, then the first sentence of a strong answer that uses the chain he "forged in life".
kf2.note: A good question asks something like how Dickens presents social responsibility through Marley's ghost. Your first sentence should link "Mankind was my business" to the chain he "forged in life". It should show the chain is the punishment for a life spent chasing wealth instead of helping others. Check that you used both quotations and named Dickens's message. If your question was only about how Marley looks, the line about mankind has nothing to answer.

cs1.tip: Link Scrooge's "decrease the surplus population" to the Victorian Context & Dickens' Purpose lesson: say which Victorian attitude Dickens attacks here and how.
cs1.note: Dickens attacks the way wealthy Victorians used economic theory as an excuse not to help the poor. "Surplus" echoes Malthusian economics and reduces people to a statistic to be managed. Dickens gives this view to his coldest character, so the reader rejects it. Fred answers it by calling people "fellow-passengers to the grave". If you only said Scrooge is mean, you missed that Dickens is targeting the attitude of a whole class, not just one man.
